study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Lin et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2023
study_identification_part.si4_title: Understanding the heterogeneity of dynamic functional connectivity patterns in first-episode drug naïve depression using normative models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Combine dynamic resting-state fMRI features with normative modeling to quantify and map individual-level heterogeneity in first-episode drug-naïve major depressive disorder (FEDN-MDD).
study_characteristics_part.sc2_study_design: Cross-sectional, multi-site observational study with normative modeling trained on healthy controls and applied to independent patients and controls from the same dataset.
study_characteristics_part.sc3_study_design_other: Healthy controls split into healthy-ICA (n=125) for network derivation, healthy-base (n=289) for normative training, and healthy-comparison (n=418) for application; patients FEDN-MDD (n=274).

rci2_hc_n.reason: HC_N refers to the normative reference cohort used to train the model; the study defines a "healthy-base" group of 289 controls used to establish the normative model.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Dynamic FC-based normative deviations distinguish distributions between FEDN-MDD and controls more than static FC; more patients show extreme supra-normal dynamic variability within networks; excluding top-5% outliers reduces case–control differences.
